description.value: The study examined whether the first prominent behavioral symptom of bvFTD, apathy or disinhibition, is associated with later neuropsychological profiles and patterns of brain atrophy, using neuropsychological measures, 3T structural MRI, whole-brain and ROI VBM, anatomical-clinical correlations, and multivariate classification.

design.value: A two-stage, cross-sectional study retrospectively classified patients according to their first-consultation symptom and then assessed them approximately three years after disease debut. Thirty healthy controls and 34 patients with probable bvFTD were evaluated; the patients comprised 18 who debuted with apathy and 16 who debuted with disinhibition. Neuropsychological, clinical, and neuroanatomical correlates were compared using group statistics, VBM, correlation analyses, factorial discriminant analysis, and support vector machine classification.

task_description.value: Neuroanatomical correlates were assessed using 3T structural images, with voxel-based morphometry used to assess brain atrophy correlates in healthy controls and the two bvFTD groups.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3T scanner with a 16-channel SENSE antenna

description.value: The anatomical and 3D T1-weighted images had TR = 7.9, TE = 3.8, ACQ matrix 220×220 pixels, voxel size 0.5×0.5×0.5 mm, and 310 sections.

Data processing and analysis were performed with VBM8 in the Statistical Parametric Mapping 8 package running under Matlab 2012b. Images were inspected for artifacts, normalized to the same stereotaxic space using the DARTEL algorithm, segmented, modulated with Jacobian determinants, and smoothed with an isotropic Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: Each image was inspected for artifacts.
The T1-weighted images were normalized to the same stereotaxic space generated from the complete data set using the DARTEL algorithm.
The images were segmented into WM and GM and non-brain voxels (CSF, skull).
All images were modulated to correct volume changes by Jacobian determinants.
Images were smoothed by convolution with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum.

model_settings.value: Whole-brain analyses compared AbvFTD and DbvFTD with healthy controls and compared AbvFTD with DbvFTD. Analyses controlled for global intracranial volume, age, gender, and length of disease duration; whole-brain comparisons were corrected with FDR at 0.001, and between-patient comparisons used FDR at 0.05.

VBM analyses were conducted using a mask centered in critical bilateral ROIs involved in bvFTD behavioral symptoms, including DLPFC, OFC, ACC, caudate, putamen, amygdala, and hippocampus. Between-group ROI analyses were corrected using FDR at 0.05.
Pearson's correlation coefficient with Sidak correction was used to identify relationships between VBM scores in ROIs and standardized neuropsychological measures in each patient group.

estimator.value: Pearson's correlation coefficient and Sidak correction

model_type.value: one-way ANOVA and chi square tests

model_settings.value: Demographic and neuropsychological data were compared between AbvFTD, DbvFTD, and controls using one-way ANOVA and chi square tests. Bonferroni post-hoc tests were used when appropriate; a one-way ANOVA assessed differences in neuropsychological measures between the two patient groups.

estimator.value: one-way ANOVA, chi square tests, and Bonferroni post-hoc tests

model_settings.value: Two FDA models were performed to classify AbvFTD and DbvFTD: one including significant neuropsychological and anatomical variables, and one including only significant anatomical variables. A final stepwise discriminant analysis used forward selection with elimination at the 5% level.

estimator.value: factorial discriminant analysis with stepwise variable selection

model_settings.value: SVM models classified AbvFTD and DbvFTD using neuropsychological measures and ROI variables, whole-brain anatomical variables, or ROI variables alone. Recursive feature elimination and Weka attribute selection were used; models used 10-fold cross-validation and optimized γ, the width of the radial basis function, and C, the error/trade-off parameter.

estimator.value: support vector machine classifier with 10-fold cross-validation

software.value: Waikato Environment for Knowledge Analysis (WEKA) suite of ML software
